newsitem.title: MEXICO: Five police killed in Mexico attacks.
newsitem.headline: Five police killed in Mexico attacks.

text.p: Armed rebels and gunmen attacked police patrols and stations in three Mexican states overnight, killing five officers and wounding several others, authorities and national media said on Friday.

Four officers died when rebels, believed to belong to the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR), ambushed a police patrol near the tourist city of Oaxaca, about 220 miles (360 km) southeast of Mexico City, state officials said. Three others were injured.

Another police officer died and two others were injured in the State of Mexico when four armed men wearing military-style uniforms rained bullets on and threw molotov cocktails at the local police station of Coacalco, just outside the limits of Mexico City, media reports said.

In a third attack in Guerrero state, armed men opened fire close to a police academy in the town of Atoyac, 50 miles (80 km) west of the tourist resort of Acapulco. No one was killed or injured in the attack, newspapers said.

Oaxaca's state government said the police patrol was forced to slow down when it came across a burning roadblock close to the village of San Pablo Maculxochitl, about 16 miles (26 km) from the capital.

"The patrol reduced speed and the people who were hiding on a bridge suddenly opened fire," Oaxaca's government said in a statement, making no direct reference to the EPR which operates in the region. Three other policemen were injured.

Little is known about the EPR, a shadowy Marxist rebel group which first appeared in Mexico in late June and vowed to topple the government of President Ernesto Zedillo. It has carried out random attacks on military and police in at least six Mexican states.

Although the Oaxaca attack bears the hallmarks of the EPR, it was not clear if the attacks in the State of Mexico and Guerrero were also carried out by the guerrillas or were the work of rogue gunmen. The EPR did not immediately claim responsibility for the attacks.
Reforma daily said the Coacalco attack, the third in the state since an EPR month-long ceasefire ended on Oct. 27, was the work of four men in a vehicle with foreign license plates.
